q1: SELECT beer.name, min_price, bar FROM beer LEFT OUTER JOIN (SELECT beer, MIN(price) AS min_price FROM serves GROUP BY beer) AS t ON beer.name = t.beer LEFT OUTER JOIN serves ON beer.name = serves.beer AND min_price = serves.price
q2: SELECT b.name, b1.beer, b1.min_price FROM (SELECT s.beer, MIN(s.price) AS min_price FROM serves AS s GROUP BY s.beer) AS b1 LEFT JOIN serves AS s ON b1.beer = s.beer AND b1.min_price = s.price LEFT JOIN bar AS b ON s.bar = b.name ORDER BY b1.beer

counterexample: INSERT INTO beer (name, brewer) VALUES ('BeerA', 'BrewerX'); INSERT INTO bar (name, address) VALUES ('BarY', 'AddressY');
explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not semantically equivalent because of the order of JOIN operations and the use of subqueries. Q1 first performs the JOIN between beer and the subquery t, and then between t and serves. Q2, on the other hand, first performs the JOIN between the subquery b1 and serves, and then between the result and bar. This difference in JOIN order can lead to different results, especially when there are NULL values involved.
counterexample_dsp: The test data should include a beer that is not served by any bar, and a bar that serves no beer. This will trigger the difference in results between Q1 and Q2.
